reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 shows low wear in a different alloy system (NiX) without Y or oxide nanocomposite mechanism. E2 describes a self-adaptive nanocomposite layer in a TiNbZrAg alloy, not CoCrFeNi with Y, and relies on a different mechanism (amorphous-crystalline, Ag nanocrystals). E3 only details test methods for CoCrFeMnNi at RT, providing no evidence for Y doping, oxide layer formation, or high-temperature behavior. Thus, the specific claims about Y-induced oxide nanocomposite lubrication across the temperature range are unsupported by the cited
premises: Y addition promotes formation of a continuous, adherent, nanocrystalline oxide layer during sliding
This oxide nanocomposite layer acts as a solid lubricant, reducing interfacial shear
The lubricious oxide layer mitigates adhesive, oxidative, and plastic wear from RT to 800 °C
The adaptive layer reduces friction coefficient by ~30% and wear rate by 1-2 orders of magnitude vs. undoped CoCrFeNi
The mechanism is effective across the full RT-800 °C range in ambient air
